From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 05:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: High 429 rate + latency spike for Clearsight prod (region: us-west-2)

Quick triage notes (logs attached):

- Root signal: per-tenant burst window parameter was unintentionally set to 60 (interpreted as 60 seconds by the runtime) when the policy author intended 60 minutes. The config change was pushed at 2027-06-29T21:50:12Z by an automated rollout.
- Effect: burst credits exhausted within ~4 minutes of peak traffic; fallback routing then kicked to the cheaper t4 model variant that doesn't have the same KV cache semantics. This caused higher per-request latency and additional 429s as token generation retried.
- Evidence: see query-logs-20270629.csv (columns: timestamp, tenant_id, code, model_variant, latency_ms) and clear correlation with the change. I've included a short screenshot of the console flag we can see (screenshot-rateconfig.png).

Immediate mitigation applied at 2027-06-30T05:03:00Z:
- Temporarily increased Clearsight burst bucket by +300% and extended burst window to 3600s (stopgap)
- Forced routing to the primary model variant for their tenant (no fallbacks)

Post-mitigation: error rate dropped to <0.5% within 90s; P95 latency returned to baseline. I'm recommending an exec escalation for two reasons: (1) this was a policy interpretation/config drift from an automated rollout that could impact SLAs broadly, and (2) we should authorize an emergency policy freeze and rollback.

Attachments: query-logs-20270629.csv, screenshot-rateconfig.png

— Connor
SRE, Redwood Inference

3) Ops/Legal: prepare the impact summary for the exec sync at 9:30am PST (incl. estimated token loss, SLA risk, number of affected tenants). Bring a recommendation for whether we should apply a company-wide hold on similar auto-rollouts until policy schema validation is added.

Also: collect the change author and the CI job that triggered the rollout. If this came from a scheduled job, escalate to platform release manager.

I'll join the 9:30am call. We should also get a short-term credit decision ready so Sean can offer it on the call.

— Marissa Cole

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:42:00 +0000
Subject: Clearsight incident update: mitigation applied and next steps

Emily — quick update after our call this morning. Thank you for your patience. In short:

- What happened: an automated policy rollout inadvertently set Clearsight's burst window to 60 (seconds) instead of 60 (minutes). When your peak traffic came, the tenant exhausted burst credits quickly and the runtime routed requests to a fallback model variant that does not share the same KV cache behavior. That sequence increased latency and produced the 429s you saw.
- What we did: Connor applied a temporary +300% burst-credit increase and forced routing to the primary model at 2027-06-30T05:03:00Z; error rate fell back to baseline within 90s. Karthik initiated rollback of the rollout and we've frozen further auto-rollouts touching quota schema until we add validation.
- Next steps:
  • We will run a focused RCA and a policy-schema validation task (owner: Karthik).
  • We propose a service credit for the affected 00:22–00:07 UTC window; I'll send formal numbers after the postmortem.
  • We will share the full postmortem (draft link attached) and the Jira SRV-2138 for tracking.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-link.txt (internal doc), SRV-2138 link in related_links above.

Again — apologies for the disruption. We value the Clearsight partnership and will follow up with concrete remediation and compensation options by tomorrow EOD.

— Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
